approach: Add one pure reading check, `check_behavior_test_design`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, wired as one `step!` line directly after `check_code_survey`. It reads only the reading's `Code survey:` assumptions, criteria and deliverables, plus the record tags compiled into athena-data's `AnyRecord`. It parses the survey into labelled clauses (`Entry point:`, `Gate order:`, `Stop gate:`, `Reuses:`, `Output:`, `Direct check:`) and judges each clause alone. (a) Entry point and gate order hold identifiers, and the stop gate equals one of the gate-order identifiers. (b) `Reuses:` names an identifier or says "no existing function". (c) `Output:` says "no new output", or names a record kind that is checked against the code (a schema tag that `AnyRecord` accepts, `AnyRecord::<Variant>` whose variant matches an accepted tag, or `check_record_file`), or names a round-trip identifier that also has a behavior criterion naming it and a deliverable that can hold the test. A bare `AnyRecord` and an unknown tag are refused. (d) Each behavior criterion has its own `Direct check:` clause that cites exactly that one criterion, holds a measurement verb, and does not measure through a skip switch or an internal-helper read. Round 4 changes: (1) the accepted record tags are read from athena-data at run time, by deserialising `{"schema": <probe>}` as `AnyRecord` and parsing serde's expected-variant list, so a made-up tag and a bare `AnyRecord` are contradictions; no records.rs edit; (2) `check_code_survey`'s missing-survey error now asks for the six labels and prints the same example, so a retry that follows it passes both steps; (3) one criterion per `Direct check:` clause, and the guide example measures its own property; (4) `steward::queued_work` and the drain are named as dependents and the CHANGELOG says queued proposed readings may need a re-read; (5) the existing `check_code_survey` tests keep their short surveys and test acceptance on `check_code_survey` directly; (6) step references renumbered; (7) the open question is marked blocking before the producer runs. The reader guide `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE` is rewritten in place to teach the labelled format with a filled-in example, and `survey_example()` extracts that example so the guide, both error texts and the tests share one source.

decisions.choice: Judge the survey by labelled clauses, not by whole-text phrase search. A clause runs from its label (case-insensitive, at the start of the text or after whitespace or a full stop) to the next label. A repeated label, or a label in a second `Code survey:` assumption, adds to the same clause. Position finding uses ASCII lowercase on whitespace-normalised original text, so identifier case (`AnyRecord`) is kept.
decisions.reason: Each part is read inside its own clause, so 'directly' or 'calls' in a description of the code cannot stand for a measurement, and the stop gate is looked up only in the `Gate order:` clause. The reading is a plain `Vec<String>` of assumptions (surveys.rs:117-124), so labels are the only structure available without changing the Reading type.

rejected.option: Whole-survey phrase search
rejected.why: A name in the list of paths read would pass as a stop gate, and 'directly' plus 'calls' anywhere would satisfy (d) for every criterion.

decisions.choice: (a): `Entry point:` holds an identifier. `Gate order:` holds at least two distinct identifiers. `Stop gate:` holds an identifier equal, after trimming backticks and `()`, to one in the gate order. An identifier is a backtick-quoted token with no whitespace, or a bare whitespace token (trailing punctuation trimmed) that contains `_` or `::` or ends in `()`. A stop gate in prose has no identifier and is refused as missing (a); a stop gate not in the order is refused as a contradiction.
decisions.reason: Single-word gate functions such as `replay` (replay.rs:365) count when backticked, and the template's names are backticked. Bare prose words are not identifiers, so 'the resolution step' names no gate.

rejected.option: Bare identifiers only (`_`, `::` or `()`)
rejected.why: Refuses real single-word functions and the template.

rejected.option: Accept a prose stop gate
rejected.why: The check cannot compare prose with the order.

decisions.choice: (b): `Reuses:` holds an identifier, or the phrase 'no existing function', or both. Refuse an absent or empty clause, or one with neither. Partial reuse ('reuses `names_record_evidence`; no existing function checks gate order') is accepted.
decisions.reason: This is the shape of this job's own reading and of the template.

decisions.choice: (c): validate record kinds against athena-data, not against a guess. `accepted_record_tags()` in surveys.rs deserialises `serde_json::json!({"schema": "athena.probe-unknown/0"})` as `athena_data::records::AnyRecord` and parses the backtick-quoted names that follow 'expected one of' in serde's unknown-variant error (the tags come from the `#[serde(tag = "schema")]` renames at records.rs:1121-1199); it is cached in a `OnceLock`. athena-core depends on athena-data and serde_json (crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml:14,22). A new `record_kind_problem(clause)` over the `Output:` clause finds: (i) every token `athena.<kind>/<n>`; each must be in the accepted set, else the clause is refused as a contradiction ('names the schema tag X, which AnyRecord does not accept'); (ii) every `AnyRecord::<Variant>`; the variant, lowercased, must equal the kind of some accepted tag with hyphens removed, or that kind followed by the version (`Candidate2` matches `athena.candidate/2`), else contradiction; (iii) `check_record_file`. The clause passes when it says 'no new output' or 'no new record' with no record or data deliverable, or holds a valid kind from (i)-(iii), or a round-trip identifier (`is_round_trip_token`, extracted from `names_record_evidence` with no behaviour change) with its two extra needs: a behavior criterion that names a round-trip token, and a deliverable that can hold the test (path has a `tests/` directory, or ends `records.rs`, or appears in the Output clause). A bare `AnyRecord` with no variant and no tag, when `names_record_evidence` is the only match, is refused as 'names AnyRecord but no record kind'. Contradiction: 'no new output' while a deliverable satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable`. The new step still calls `names_record_evidence(clause)` first as the gate for any record evidence, so it reuses that function.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The accepted kinds are in the code and reachable from athena-core with no edit to records.rs, so the check can refuse an unknown tag as a contradiction, as criterion 3 asks. The variant-to-tag mapping is by name convention, which holds for every variant at records.rs:1124-1198; a test pins a sample of variants and the tag list. A test also pins that the probe returns the list (at least 40 tags including `athena.request/1` and `athena.candidate/2`), so a serde message change fails a test and not a reading. The check still cannot confirm that a function or file named elsewhere in the survey exists; the doc comment says so.

decisions.choice: (d): each behavior criterion needs its own `Direct check:` clause. A clause cites exactly one criterion number (`criterion 2`). A clause with no number counts for the single behavior criterion only when the reading has exactly one. A clause that cites more than one number, a list ('criteria 2 and 3') or a range ('criteria 1-4', counted as every number in it), is refused with 'one direct check covers N criteria; write one Direct check clause per criterion'. Each clause must hold a measurement verb (`count`, `counts`, `counting`, `counted`, `asserts`, `asserting`, `compares`, `observes`). Uncovered criterion numbers are listed in the error.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 6. The request asks for a direct check for each claimed property; one criterion per clause is simpler than an arbitrary cap of two and closes the range bypass. A clause can still state a measurement that is untrue; the doc comment says so, and the plan critic and verifier judge it.

rejected.option: Allow up to two criteria per clause
rejected.why: An arbitrary number; both criteria state separate measurements.

rejected.option: One global pair of words ('directly' plus 'calls')
rejected.why: Prose about the code satisfies it, and one statement covers any number of criteria.

decisions.choice: Skip-switch and internal-helper contradictions, scoped to the means of measurement. Phrases: `skip switch`, `skip flag`, `test-only switch`, `--skip`, `internal helper`, `private helper`. Split the text into segments at commas, semicolons, full stops and the word `but`. In a `Direct check:` clause an occurrence counts unless a negator (`no`, `not`, `never`, `without`, `nor`, `instead of`) stands earlier in the SAME segment. Refusal words (`refuse`, `refused`, `reject`) do not cancel, except a refusal verb within two words right before the phrase ('refuses a skip switch'). In a behavior criterion an occurrence counts only when a measuring-means phrase (`through`, `via`, `using`, `by reading`, `by inspecting`, `measured/checked/verified/tested` followed by `by` or `with`) is within 4 words before it in the same segment and no negator precedes it in that segment. A bare `read` is not a means phrase.
decisions.reason: A single early `not` or `refused` no longer disables the check for the whole clause, so 'Direct check: criterion 2 asserts the reading is refused, measured through a skip switch' is refused. The request's wording, the template, and this job's own criterion 3 are accepted. Limit: a criterion that describes a refusal fixture with 'through a skip switch' is refused and must be reworded; the doc comment states it.

rejected.option: A negator or refusal word anywhere earlier in the clause cancels
rejected.why: One early 'refused' or 'not' empties the check for refusal-rule readings.

rejected.option: Refuse on any mention
rejected.why: Refuses the sentence the reader is asked to write.

risks.risk: The real newly refused share exceeds the declared 20% plus 5 points, so the host replay holds the job. Records are not in the snapshot, so no step can measure it.
risks.mitigation: The check is not loosened to fit the number. The fixture test proves the arithmetic only. The share is an estimate until the host replay records it. The open question is marked blocking so Athena can re-read with a declared share and a reason sentence before a producer run is spent.

risks.risk: The check cannot see the repository: it cannot tell that a named function does not exist, or that a stated measurement is untrue. It does read the record tags from athena-data.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment says so, like `check_history_fixture` and `check_records_measure`. `check_reading_references` still compares paths when files are known. The planner's dependents list, the plan critic and the verifier guard function-level facts.

risks.risk: The accepted-tag list is read from serde's unknown-variant message, and the variant-to-tag mapping is by name convention; a serde message change or an irregular variant name would break it.
risks.mitigation: `accepted_record_tags_come_from_anyrecord` pins the list (at least 40 tags, with named examples) and the mapping for sample variants, so a change fails a test and not a reading. If the probe returned nothing the check would refuse every typed-record Output, which the pin test catches at once.

risks.risk: Labelled clauses make the check strict about format; a reader that writes the right content without the labels is refused.
risks.mitigation: The reader guide teaches the labels with a filled-in example, and `check_code_survey`'s error now prints the same example, so even the retry after the first refusal can comply. A test proves the example and the error's template pass. Labels match in any case and parts may spread over several `Code survey:` assumptions.

risks.risk: The guide rewrite pushes the reading-rules section over the test constants `READING_RULES_BASELINE_BYTES` and `< 3150`.
risks.mitigation: Trim first. Otherwise raise both with a comment giving the reason. They are test constants and not the prompt budget; no prompt file is edited and the reader set stays at 1998 of 2000.

risks.risk: A criterion that describes a refusal fixture with a means phrase ('through a skip switch') is refused as a contradiction (false positive).
risks.mitigation: The means list is narrow and a bare `read` is excluded, so this job's own criteria pass (fixture). The doc comment states the limit, and the error says to reword.

risks.risk: One criterion per `Direct check:` clause makes a reading with many behavior criteria longer.
risks.mitigation: The error names the rule and the uncovered numbers; the guide example shows the form. A short clause per criterion is what the request asks for.

risks.risk: Fixture drift: tests that go through the whole gate with the short survey are refused first by the new step.
risks.mitigation: Steps 5 and 9 replace each such survey. The producer greps `Code survey:` and `SURVEY` in reading.rs and refusal_corpus.rs and runs `cargo test -p athena-core` before finishing.

risks.risk: Stored proposed code readings accepted under the old rules leave the drain batch until a person runs `athena go`.
risks.mitigation: Intended: one definition of an accepted reading. The CHANGELOG says queued proposed readings may need a re-read; `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` shows the drain still behaves for readings that pass.

risks.risk: status.rs and replay.rs are listed deliverables but need no change.
risks.mitigation: The producer report says why for each: stats key on the step name string, and replay already holds a declared share plus 5 points.
